sections.title: Model overview and intended purpose
sections.text: Python Gradient Boosting (python-gradient-boosting) is a challenger model that predicts the target default.payment.next.month and is compared against the production default model; per the facts provided, it informs but does not drive decisions, though this business purpose is recorded as inferred. It is assigned risk tier 2. It uses the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset (30,000 records of credit-card clients in Taiwan, payment history April to September 2005), which is described as public demonstration data only and not representative of a UK bank's current portfolio. The business owner, intended use and decision context are not documented.

sections.title: Algorithm and methodology
sections.text: The model is a scikit-learn GradientBoostingClassifier using library default hyperparameters except random_state set to a seed (default 42), with 21 predictors covering credit limit, education, marital status, repayment status (PAY_0, PAY_2 to PAY_6), bill amounts and payment amounts; ID, SEX and AGE are excluded from the predictors. Preprocessing renames the target column, drops ID, drops rows with missing values on the workbook load path, validates the official UCI data (30,000 rows, 25 columns, no missing values, default rate between 20% and 24%), and casts the target to int; no scaling or encoding is applied. Data is split with a stratified train/test split (test_size=0.2, random_state=42), and a decision threshold of 0.5 is recorded, although the input feature list, train fraction and threshold are marked as inferred. The approved threshold and its rationale, and the hyperparameter selection rationale, are not documented.

sections.title: Limitations and assumptions
sections.text: No hyperparameter tuning or class imbalance handling is applied, unlike the random forest, which uses class_weight='balanced'. SEX and AGE are excluded on the assumption that this addresses fairness, but proxy variables such as EDUCATION and MARRIAGE remain among the predictors, and fairness test results and tolerances are not documented. A synthetic demo dataset may be used when UCI data is unavailable, which would change the feature set, and the data path used in production is not documented. Validation metrics, acceptance criteria, PSI results, monitoring and retraining plans, model version and deployment details are not documented.
